exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I'm lactose intolerant. Which brand or product should I choose, and why?
reviewed_answer:
Choose LACTAID Lactose-Free Cottage Cheese if you want the safest, most reliable option in U.S. stores. It is specifically labeled lactose-free because it contains lactase enzyme, which breaks milk’s lactose into easier-to-digest sugars; it also has 13 g protein per 1/2 cup.

Best pick

LACTAID Cottage Cheese, 4% milkfat, 16 oz

Explicitly lactose-free, so it avoids the guesswork of ordinary cottage cheese.

The added lactase converts lactose into glucose and galactose, which people with lactose intolerance generally digest more easily.

It is a conventional dairy cottage cheese—not dairy-free—so it is appropriate for lactose intolerance, not a milk allergy.

Good alternative

Good Culture Simply Lactose-Free Cottage Cheese, 2% milkfat, 15 oz is another clearly labeled lactose-free choice, with a thick, high-protein style.

Product	Why choose it	Watch for
LACTAID Lactose-Free Cottage Cheese	Purpose-made lactose-free option; widely available; 13 g protein per 1/2 cup. 
	4% milkfat; some reviewers note a slightly tangy flavor. 

Good Culture Lactose-Free Cottage Cheese	Labeled lactose-free and creamy/high-protein. 
	Availability varies by store.
Regular cottage cheese	Lower in lactose than milk, roughly 1–6 g per serving, and some people tolerate small portions. 
	Not lactose-free; avoid if you react to small amounts. 
What to avoid

Do not assume “low-fat,” “organic,” “high-protein,” or “live cultures” means lactose-free. Regular cottage cheese still contains lactose, though usually less than milk; if you are sensitive, choose a package that explicitly says “lactose-free” on the front label.

If you are in [name and location withheld], LACTAID is the easiest first choice to look for at Target, Kroger, Harris Teeter, or Walmart; Target lists the 16 oz LACTAID 4% cottage cheese as lactose-free.
